_note: Draft by Claude, levels 1-2 only. Jerry to review. Each rule id is also a mistake 'tag' in the AI feedback. severity: 'major' = wrong meaning or core grammar (sends the word back to box 1 in spaced repetition); 'minor' = accents, small spelling, punctuation. The AI uses this file as its reference so explanations stay consistent. 'explain' is the plain-English line the AI should build its short_explanation from.

rules.explain: Every French noun is masculine or feminine. Use le / un for masculine and la / une for feminine.

rules.topic: le / la become l' before a vowel or silent h
rules.explain: Before a vowel or a silent h, le and la shorten to l'.
In French a noun almost always needs a small word in front of it, like le, une or des.
For an amount of something you can't count, like bread or water, use du, de la or de l'.
wrong: Je bois l'eau tous les jours.

rules.topic: un / une / du / des become de after a negative
rules.explain: After ne ... pas, un, une, du, de la and des change to de (or d').
wrong: Il ne boit pas de l'eau.

rules.topic: à + le = au, de + le = du
rules.explain: à le always becomes au, and à les becomes aux. de le becomes du, and de les becomes des.
être goes: je suis, tu es, il/elle/on est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont.
avoir goes: j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.

rules.topic: avoir for age, hunger, thirst, cold...
rules.explain: French uses avoir (to have), not être, for age, hunger, thirst, being cold or hot, and being afraid.
For -er verbs, remove -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

rules.topic: Common irregular verbs in the present (aller, faire, prendre, vouloir, pouvoir...)
rules.explain: Some very common verbs don't follow the normal pattern and have to be learned, like je vais, je fais, je prends, je veux, je peux.
The verb ending must match who is doing the action (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils).

rules.topic: je becomes j' before a vowel
rules.explain: Before a vowel or a silent h, je shortens to j'.
An adjective changes to match its noun: add -e for feminine and -s for plural.

rules.topic: Words about yourself match your own gender
rules.explain: When you talk about yourself, adjectives and past forms with être match you: a woman writes je suis fatiguée and je suis allée, a man writes je suis fatigué and je suis allé.

rules.topic: Most adjectives go after the noun
rules.explain: Most adjectives go after the noun. A few short common ones (grand, petit, bon, beau, jeune, vieux, nouveau) go before it.

rules.topic: mon / ma / mes match the thing owned
rules.explain: mon, ma and mes match the thing you own, not the owner. Use mon before a feminine word that starts with a vowel (mon amie).
Put ne before the verb and pas after it. ne becomes n' before a vowel. (In casual speech people drop ne, but in writing keep it.)
correct: Je ne mange pas de viande.
wrong: Je mange pas ne de viande.
Il ne aime pas le froid.

rules.topic: Asking questions (est-ce que, rising tone, question words)
rules.explain: Ask with est-ce que + normal sentence, or a normal sentence ending in '?'. Question words go first: Où est-ce que..., or at the end in casual speech: Tu vas où ?
où = where, quand = when, combien = how much / how many, pourquoi = why, comment = how, qui = who, quoi / qu'est-ce que = what.
wrong: Quand tu pars ? (when you meant why)

rules.topic: il y a (there is / there are)
rules.explain: 'There is' and 'there are' are both il y a. It never changes for plural.
correct: Il y a des chats dans le jardin.
Il n'y a pas de pain.
wrong: Il y ont des chats dans le jardin.

rules.topic: Prepositions of place (à, en, au, dans, chez)
rules.explain: Use à for cities, en for feminine countries, au for masculine countries, dans for 'inside', chez for 'at someone's place'.

rules.topic: Time expressions (le lundi, à 8 heures, en juin)
rules.explain: Use à for clock time, en for months and years, and le + day for 'every Monday'. Use no word at all for 'this Monday'.

rules.topic: Second verb stays in the infinitive (aimer, vouloir, pouvoir + infinitive)
rules.explain: When two verbs follow each other, only the first changes. The second stays in its basic form (manger, aller).
Most verbs use avoir in the past (j'ai mangé). Movement verbs like aller, venir, partir, arriver, and reflexive verbs, use être (je suis allé).
The past form of -er verbs ends in -é (mangé). Many common verbs are irregular: fait, pris, vu, bu, eu, été, dit, écrit, lu, mis.
With être, the past form matches the subject: add -e for a woman and -s for plural.
To say what you're going to do, use aller in the present + the basic form of the verb: je vais manger.

rules.topic: devoir / pouvoir / vouloir / avoir envie de
rules.explain: je dois = I must, je peux = I can, je veux = I want, j'ai envie de = I feel like. The next verb stays in its basic form.

Verbs with 'se' (se lever, s'habiller) are actions you do to yourself: 'lever' is to lift, 'se lever' is to lift yourself, so to get up. 'se' changes with the person: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons. In the past they use être: je me suis levé(e).
correct: Je me lève à sept heures.

rules.topic: Linking ideas: mais, et, donc, parce que, quand
rules.explain: mais = but, donc = so, parce que = because, quand = when. parce que becomes parce qu' before a vowel.
correct: Je reste ici parce qu'il pleut.
Il est fatigué, donc il dort.
wrong: Je reste ici parce que il pleut.
Il est fatigué, mais il dort. (when you meant 'so')

rules.explain: quel (which / what) matches its noun: quel for masculine, quelle for feminine, and add -s for plural.
A normal French sentence goes subject + verb + the rest, like in English.
correct: Le matin, je bois un café.
Je bois un café le matin.
wrong: Le matin bois je un café.

rules.explain: The word you used means something else in French, or is an English word written in a French way.
correct: Je vais à la bibliothèque pour emprunter un livre.
wrong: Je vais à la librairie pour emprunter un livre.

rules.explain: A missing or wrong accent, or a small typo, that doesn't change which word it is.
Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop, or with '?' for a question. French puts a space before ? ! : ;.
Use only when no other tag fits. Jerry reviews these to decide whether to add a new rule.
